known_limitations: REINDEX REQUIRED FOR EFFECT: start_line and end_line are persisted at index time and search does not recompute them, so an index built before this commit keeps its blank-padded spans indefinitely and D4 has no effect until the index is rebuilt. The schema version is unchanged at 1.0.0 and nothing rejects a stale index, so the release procedure has to guarantee the rebuild. Chunk BODIES are unchanged, so the stale-index effect is limited to printed citation ranges. Raised by Codex.

blocking.why_it_blocks: these are the receipt's own named base-LOW examples, and the package exists to stop contentless questions being answered at full confidence. On this class the candidate is worse than the base it repairs, and it was disclosed nowhere until Agent C measured it.

escalation.root_cause: D3 and D5 are coupled and cannot be separated. deterministic_evidence_strength returns HIGH whenever ANY row matched all_terms, with no regard to how few or how generic those terms are. So any change that shrinks a question's term set can promote its strength. Removing the fallback silenced legitimate questions; narrowing it promotes contentless ones. Neither edit to query_terms can be correct while the strength contract rewards smaller term sets.
escalation.what_is_finished: D4. Its source hunk is byte-identical across two Agent C passes, its five pins are live, every chunk shape was verified under base and candidate, and the only difference it makes to the index is start_line/end_line on 17 of 21 rows.
escalation.what_is_not: D3. Three formulations have now been tried - fallback to all words (base, answers 'the' at HIGH), no fallback (silences 'root cause'), fallback to non-stopwords (promotes 'show me the notes' to HIGH) - and each trades one class of wrong answer for another.
recommended_next: Split again: merge D4 on its own. It is finished, twice verified, and independently valuable.

Treat D3 and D5 as ONE package. Fix the strength contract first - all_terms over one or two generic terms should not be HIGH - and only then decide what query_terms should do, because until then every query_terms change moves strength around as a side effect.
If D3 is wanted sooner than that, the base behaviour is the safest of the three: it answers contentless questions, but at LOW, not HIGH, for the multi-word cases.
